methods.rationale: 9 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Floodbase, a Series A climate and energy company founded by Bessie Schwarz and Dr. Beth Tellman, has raised $17M to date. The valuation universe comprises 9 private peers in Climate & Energy alongside 1 public comparable (LNZA), though the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private comps with similar valuation tiers to support peer-median triangulation.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology applies. Using the $17M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to the next institutional stage yields $34M. This method represents the sole quantitative anchor available, as the peer-median approach requires minimum 3 comparable data points at matching stage and tier—a threshold not met by the narrowly filtered Climate & Energy cohort.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $29M to $39M, centered on $34M. This range reflects reasonable sensitivity around the 2.0x multiplier (±15%) applied to the $17M base. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of stage-progression multiples for early-stage climate tech, the absence of direct peer comparables at Floodbase's development and financing tier, and limited visibility into unit economics or go-to-market traction. Any refined valuation would benefit from additional same-stage private comps or disclosed metrics (ARR, customer concentration, burn rate) from the broader Climate & Energy peer set.
